reasoning: The document shows strong content preservation but suffers from multiple structural defects that block auto-approval. Specifically, the heading hierarchy is broken, 10 hyperlinks are displaced as standalone elements, and 36 header/footer elements were erroneously retained in the output. These issues, along with missing images and corrupted multi-page tables, require human correction.

concerns.analysis: There are inconsistent heading levels assigned to identically styled sibling sub-sections in the PDF. Under the "Collaborating and Applying GIS Technology" section, the first sub-section "Census Collaboration" on Page 20 is correctly extracted as an H3. However, the subsequent sub-sections on Page 21 with the exact same visual styling (underlined text) are extracted as H2s, which breaks the document's logical hierarchy. The same inconsistency occurs with bold sub-headings on Pages 23-25.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: "GIS Technology for State Agencies" on Page 21, which is an underlined sub-section identically styled to "Census Collaboration" on Page 20.
concerns.output_quote: Extracted as `{"type": "heading", "level": 2, "text": "GIS Technology for State Agencies"}`, making it a sibling to its parent heading instead of an H3.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 10 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=10, examples=['http://data.nconemap.com', 'http://data.nconemap.com/', 'http://data.nconemap.com']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.
header_footer_count=36. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

The pipeline repeatedly extracts explicit URLs inline within paragraphs and then duplicates them by appending them as standalone link objects at the very end of the page's content array. This happens on Pages 4, 6, and 25.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: The text "NC OneMap (http://data.nconemap.com), a priority initiative..." on Page 4.
concerns.output_quote: The URL is extracted inline, and then duplicated at the end of the page array as `{"type": "link", "text": "(http://data.nconemap.com)", "url": "http://data.nconemap.com/"}`.

concerns.analysis: The pipeline incorrectly splits continuous tables that span multiple pages into separate table objects. This violates the structural requirement for continuous tables, particularly when the resulting separate table object lacks header rows. The table in Appendix C spans Pages 36, 37, and 38. The output merges rows from 36 and 37 into one table object, but then creates a completely separate, headless table object for the rows on Page 38.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: The continuous data table in Appendix C spanning pages 36, 37, and 38.
concerns.output_quote: A separate table object is created on Page 38 (`{"type": "table", "cells": [{"text": "Shellfish Growing Areas"...}]}`) rather than continuing the table from Page 36, severing the data from its column headers.

concerns.analysis: A comparison between the source PDF and the rendered HTML indicates that some meaningful images are missing in the output. The source document contains an image on page 17 demonstrating Nags Head imagery, as well as an image on page 19 labeled 'Figure 7. NC Parcels Project'. Neither of these images, nor their respective captions, appear anywhere in the HTML output.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 19 features a map image with the caption 'Figure 7. NC Parcels Project, Example Where Four Counties Meet'. Page 17 features an image with the caption 'Imagery in Nags Head, NC'.
concerns.output_quote: The HTML completely omits both the image for Figure 7 and the image for Nags Head, featuring no corresponding tags or caption text.
